title: Incorrect behavior on Windows with dylibs and ThinLTO
body: On Windows, I cloned https://github.com/TheBevyFlock/bevy_quickstart and ran `cargo run --release`. Instead of running normally, it panicked inside the standard library with `internal error: entered unreachable code: state is never set to invalid values`. I reproduced this with rustc 1.81.0-nightly (5affbb171 2024-07-18), targeting x86_64-pc-windows-msvc with LLVM 18.1.7. I included the backtrace and a screenshot.

symptoms_visible: Running `cargo run --release` for bevy_quickstart on Windows panics in `std::sync::once` with `internal error: entered unreachable code: state is never set to invalid values`.
N0.label: N0 Windows release panic reported

symptoms_visible: The panic occurs in the release build but not in debug mode.
My release profile uses one codegen unit, ThinLTO, size optimization, and stripped debug information.
N1.label: N1 release configuration isolated

symptoms_visible: The optimized program still crashes when I replace ThinLTO with full LTO.
Current nightly reaches the `state is never set to invalid values` panic, while stable reaches `state_and_queue.addr() & STATE_MASK == RUNNING` in a different `Once` implementation.
N2.label: N2 LTO variants tested

symptoms_visible: A small reproducer without Bevy still crashes when the dylib is merely linked, even though the executable does not need to call anything from it.
The unattended bisect reports nightly-2022-11-09 as working and nightly-2022-11-10 as failing.
N3.label: N3 minimal reproducer and regression range obtained

symptoms_visible: With the proposed assertion enabled, the assertion passes but the reproducer still crashes.
With commit 296489c89268e56abb8f6050842d006b16ed4f09 reverted in the test compiler, the reproducer no longer crashes.
N4.label: N4 candidate compiler change tested

symptoms_visible: I retested after the fixes and the original reproducer looks good; the standard-library `Once` panic no longer occurs.
N_terminal.label: terminal reporter confirmed fixed

question_patterns: Does the same project reproduce in a debug build, or only with the release profile?
Can you compare `cargo run` with `cargo run --release`?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It does not reproduce in debug mode; I see the panic in the release build.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It crashes with the identical panic in both debug and release builds.

question_patterns: Does the release profile have any custom optimization or linking settings?
Can you paste the relevant `[profile.release]` section?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The release profile is custom: `codegen-units = 1`, `lto = "thin"`, `opt-level = "s"`, and `strip = "debuginfo"`. I don't yet know which setting matters.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: There are no custom release settings; this happens with Cargo's default release profile and with LTO disabled.
The same profile is used, except debug information is not stripped.

edges.comment: Thread c11-c13: participant2 observed that debug mode did not reproduce, and the reporter supplied the custom release profile. The observation is folded into the affected user side; no system change is retained.

question_patterns: Can you replace the current LTO mode with full LTO and report whether the optimized program still crashes?
Please compare the release build under the two LTO modes.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tested both `lto = "thin"` and `lto = true`. The optimized program crashes with either setting.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Full LTO runs correctly; only the ThinLTO configuration crashes.
Both modes still crash, but full LTO takes longer before reaching the panic.

question_patterns: Can you reproduce this with both stable Rust and the current nightly, and paste the exact panic from each?
Do older and current compiler builds fail at the same place and with the same message?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: On current nightly I get `internal error: entered unreachable code: state is never set to invalid values`. On stable I get `assertion failed: state_and_queue.addr() & STATE_MASK == RUNNING`. They are different messages from different `Once` implementations.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Stable runs the program correctly and only the latest nightly crashes.

edges.comment: Thread c14-c32: participant3 suggested the configuration probe; participants2, 3, and 5 reproduced the two raw panic forms. Their affected Windows runs are folded into one simulated user side. The conclusion that this implicates dylib/linkage rather than either `Once` implementation remains engineer-side.

question_patterns: Can you reduce this to a small project that does not depend on Bevy?
Can you provide a minimal reproducer showing the dynamic-library setup?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I reduced it to https://github.com/bash/rust-dylib-crash. It does not involve Bevy, and the dylib setup is modeled after Bevy's.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I can only reproduce it inside Bevy after its scheduling and asset systems initialize; a standalone dylib project works.

question_patterns: Can you run `cargo-bisect-rustc` on the minimized project and paste its raw range output?
Please find the last working and first failing nightly with the standalone reproducer.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The unattended run searched nightly-2020-01-01 through nightly-2024-07-19 and printed `Regression in nightly-2022-11-10`. It reports 2022-11-09 at commit 85f4f41deb1557ca8ab228319d33003dd2f20f45 and 2022-11-10 at e75aab045fc476f176a58c408f6b06f0e275c6e1.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The minimized project works on every historical nightly and starts failing only with the 2024-07-18 nightly.
The run produces the same 2022-11-09 to 2022-11-10 range from a shorter set of starting dates.

edges.comment: Thread c34-c42: participant5/bash produced the standalone reproducer and raw cargo-bisect-rustc output; participant2 observed that the dylib only had to be present. These affected-user contributions are folded into the simulated user side. Identifying a specific change inside the reported nightly range is not placed in the user's answer.

question_patterns: Can you build the compiler with the proposed diagnostic assertion enabled and report both the assertion result and the reproducer result?
Please test the instrumented compiler against the minimized project.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I finished a stage1 build with the proposed assertion. The assertion is reached and passes, but the reproducer still crashes.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The new assertion fails before linking the reproducer.

question_patterns: Can you test a compiler build that reverts the candidate change and report whether the minimal reproducer still crashes?
Please compare the reproducer with the candidate change present and reverted.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. Reverting 296489c89268e56abb8f6050842d006b16ed4f09 causes the reproducer not to crash.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The reproducer crashes identically after the candidate change is reverted.
The reverted compiler also avoids the crash when built as stage2 instead of stage1.

edges.comment: Thread c43-c48: participant1 requested the instrumented and reverted compiler tests; participant2 built both and reported the raw outcomes. This is pre-landing candidate-build verification and therefore remains a measurement clarification.

solution.intent: Fix the Windows dylib/LTO interaction rather than changing `std::sync::Once`: stop Cargo from passing linker-plugin LTO for a ThinLTO build involving dylibs, and restore correct compiler handling of dylib linkage by reverting the regressing codegen behavior; then ask the reporter to retest a toolchain containing the fixes.
solution.concrete_example: Cargo was incorrectly passing `-C linker-plugin-lto` for ThinLTO even when dylibs were involved, a combination that is unsupported and was not being rejected correctly. Together with reverting the earlier dylib-linkage codegen change and applying the accompanying compiler corrections, the minimized project and Bevy template ran with both rust-lld and link. Ask the original reporter to rerun the reproducer on a toolchain containing those fixes.
solution.inference_hint: The bisect output only supplies the nightly range, and the candidate-build tests only report whether the crash occurs. Engineers mapped that evidence to the earlier dylib-linkage codegen change and later established that Cargo was incorrectly passing `-C linker-plugin-lto` for ThinLTO when dylibs were involved. Those causal conclusions must be inferred rather than attributed to the reporter.

edges.comment: Thread c49-c55: maintainers diagnosed the dylib/linkage and LTO interaction, later reported that correcting Cargo's linker-plugin-LTO behavior plus the compiler changes made the repositories work, and asked the original reporter to confirm. The reporter eventually replied `LGTM :)`, so terminal resolution is based on affected-reporter confirmation rather than maintainer landing status alone.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause as a Windows dylib/LTO linkage failure: Cargo incorrectly passed linker-plugin LTO for ThinLTO when dylibs were involved, interacting with regressed compiler handling of dylib linkage and causing invalid memory to be observed inside otherwise-correct `Once` implementations.
The diagnosis must be grounded in the release-only behavior, both LTO-mode tests, standalone dylib reproducer, raw nightly bisection range, and the compiler-revert test.

Must not diagnose the unreachable branch or assertion as a defect in `std::sync::Once`; different stable and nightly implementations failed because bad dylib/linkage output led them to observe invalid state.
Must not present switching from ThinLTO to full LTO as the fix, because the reproducer crashed under both settings.

Must ask the original reporter to verify a toolchain containing the fixes and must not declare resolution before that retest; the thread reaches resolution when the reporter later confirms it looks good.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable Rust and Bevy user who can edit Cargo profiles, collect full backtraces, compare compiler versions, and coordinate more expensive compiler tests; additional affected contributors with compiler-building and bisection experience are folded into the user side.
persona_hint.communication_style: Cooperative and candid about uncertainty; supplies exact commands, configuration snippets, panic text, and links; corrects earlier assumptions when maintainers distinguish superficially similar failures.
